resources.string: View PSS, RSS, swap, and the memory breakdown for the main process
The metrics cover the main process. Background audio and WebView renderers can run in separate processes.

Proportional Set Size, the memory attributed proportionally to this process. Private pages count in full, and shared pages are split among the processes using them. For example, two processes sharing 20 MiB each count 10 MiB. Android can also include a proportional share of swapped pages in total PSS.
Resident Set Size, the size of pages currently resident in physical memory. Every process using a shared page counts it in full.
The total size of pages from this process that have been moved to swap. Devices using zRAM store these pages in compressed form.
The heap managed by the Android runtime, mainly for Kotlin and Java objects.
Heap memory allocated through the native allocator, such as allocations made by C/C++ libraries.
Program code and static resources mapped into the process, such as APKs, DEX files, shared libraries, and fonts.
Memory threads use for function calls and local variables.
Graphics buffers and rendering memory attributed to the process by Android.
Private memory outside the preceding categories, such as some runtime overhead.
Memory Android attributes to the system and shared mappings, such as shared pages from runtime libraries and framework code.
One KiB equals 1,024 bytes. One MiB equals 1,024 KiB.
Show memory usage on other pages. Tap to expand.
